title: Normalized Hom and bidual comparison for the explicit adic section equivalence
statement: For each prime ℓ and scheme X, the explicitly constructed comparisonModuleFunctor identifies native internal Hom with slice-Hom naturally in both variables; native evaluation is evaluation on the identity slice, and the native bidual transpose has the stated restriction formula.

source.place: Tags 03EO and 0E8H; slice-Hom currying, evaluation, and bidual transpose.

proof.text: Use the normalized tensor comparison and the explicit section-module functor. Curry the inverse tensor comparison followed by the image of the native tensor-Hom counit, using the general-site tensor–slice-Hom equivalence. On every further slice this evaluates native evaluation on the restricted Hom section and the given module section.

For each native module P, composition with this Hom comparison identifies with the composite of the native tensor-Hom bijection, full faithfulness of the section-module functor, precomposition by the tensor comparison isomorphism, and general-site currying. Thus these maps are bijective. Essential surjectivity supplies the same assertion for every section-module sheaf, and Yoneda implies that the comparison is invertible. The native evaluation naturality equations give naturality in both variables on every slice.

Evaluation on the identity slice removes the identity restriction and gives the required evaluation formula. Evaluate the proved native bidual transpose on a pure tensor; the lax braided sheaf-to-presheaf functor interchanges its factors. Naturality of the bidual with restriction and the comparison formula on each further slice then give the stated bidual section formula.
